data.name: BANANO BROS.
data.detailed_description:
Banano Bros is a retro arcade game inspired by the old time classics of the 80's. This game is a vertical endless runner with procedurally generated obstacles where your only goal is trying to beat your own record and playing with your friends.

Key Features

  • Play in singleplayer, local cooperative multiplayer or local versus multiplayer.
  • Attract your partner to you to save him from death or kill him in versus mode.
  • Climb to the clouds and collect bananos to multiply your score.
  • Dodge insects and coconuts.
  • Retro pixel graphics inspired in the old game systems.
  • Awesome retro music made by the artist Ozzed.
  • Steam archievements.
  • Compatible with gamepad.

reviews.review:
BANANO BROS. is a lightweight arcade experience that embraces the straightforward design philosophy of classic games, where the objective is immediately understandable and improvement comes from repeated attempts. Developed and published by Project Purity Team, the game places you in control of a monkey determined to climb as high as possible while collecting bananas and surviving an increasingly troublesome assortment of obstacles. It does not burden the concept with an elaborate story or complicated progression systems. Instead, everything revolves around movement, survival, collecting, and earning a better score.

The basic gameplay works as a vertically focused endless runner. Your character continually works upward while hazards such as insects and coconuts threaten to bring the attempt to an abrupt end. Bananas scattered along the route provide an additional incentive to take risks, as collecting them contributes to increasing the score multiplier. This creates a pleasant balance between simply staying alive and deliberately putting yourself in less comfortable positions to maximize points. The controls and rules are simple enough to understand almost immediately, allowing the challenge to come primarily from execution rather than learning complicated mechanics.

Procedurally generated obstacles give individual runs some variation. You cannot rely entirely on memorizing one fixed sequence, so attention and reactions remain important as you climb. The randomization does not completely prevent repetition, however. The fundamental actions remain largely unchanged throughout the experience, meaning players who are not interested in score chasing may feel that they have seen most of what the game offers relatively quickly. For arcade enthusiasts, this simplicity can instead become part of the attraction, since every failure provides another opportunity to restart and improve.

Collecting bananas and pursuing higher scores are supported by Steam leaderboards, giving competitive players a clear reason to continue practicing. Rather than completing a traditional campaign and putting the game aside, the goal becomes improving efficiency and surviving longer. Steam achievements provide another collection of objectives to pursue. These additions do not radically expand the underlying gameplay, but they complement the arcade structure and give dedicated players measurable milestones beyond their personal best.

Local multiplayer adds considerably more personality to the concept. Cooperative play lets two players tackle the climbing challenge together, introducing an unusual interaction where one monkey can attract the other. This can become a useful rescue technique when a partner gets into trouble. The versus mode takes that same mechanic and gives it a mischievous purpose, allowing players to interfere with one another and potentially turn an otherwise routine climb into a chaotic competition. Remote Play Together further increases the usefulness of these local multiplayer modes by allowing them to be enjoyed remotely.

The visual presentation deliberately adopts an old-school pixel-art style rather than attempting anything technically ambitious. Characters, bananas, platforms, and dangers are presented clearly enough that the player can quickly interpret what is happening during faster sections. The aesthetic suits the uncomplicated mechanics and helps establish the feeling of playing a small retro arcade title. The soundtrack by Ozzed reinforces that atmosphere with music that fits naturally alongside the energetic, score-driven action.

The greatest limitation is the amount of mechanical depth available after the initial novelty fades. There are no expansive environments to explore, deep character systems to master, or substantial narrative developments waiting after hours of play. Procedural generation changes obstacle arrangements, but the overall objective remains consistent from one run to another. As a result, BANANO BROS. is better suited to short sessions than marathon play. Someone who enjoys endlessly improving a score can get significantly more mileage from it than someone primarily motivated by unlocking new content.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially categorized as Playable rather than fully Verified. Performance with the default graphics configuration is considered suitable, and the game can run successfully on SteamOS. However, handheld players should expect compromises. Some functionality is not fully accessible through the default controller configuration, touchscreen interaction or a community controller layout may occasionally be useful, and text entry can require manually opening the virtual keyboard. Some interface text may also appear small, while certain prompts can display keyboard, mouse, or non-Steam Deck controller icons. It is therefore functional on the Deck, but the experience is less seamless than a fully optimized handheld release.

Overall, BANANO BROS. understands the kind of experience it wants to provide and rarely tries to become something larger. It is an uncomplicated retro arcade game centered on climbing, collecting bananas, avoiding hazards, and pushing for better scores. Procedural challenges and leaderboards strengthen the replay-oriented structure, while cooperative and competitive multiplayer provide the most interesting variations on the core formula. Its limited depth and repetitive nature prevent it from becoming a particularly substantial experience, but as a quick arcade diversion, especially with another player involved, it has an appealing simplicity.

Rating: 7/10
